questions.stem_latex:
At an airport, luggage is weighed at check-in to ensure that it meets the airlines strict requirements.

The mass of each piece of luggage, in kilograms, is modelled by a continuous random variable X, whose probability density function is

$$f(x)=\begin{cases} kx^2(30-x) & 0\le x\le 30\\ 0 & \text{elsewhere}\end{cases}$$

parts.label: i
parts.latex: Find the value of $k$.

parts.label: ii
parts.latex:
An airline allows each passenger one piece of luggage free of charge if it weighs 23 kg or less and refuses to carry a bag if the single bag weighs more than 30kg.

They charge \$40 excess fee for every kilogram, or part thereof, a bag is over the 23kg.

What is the probability that a passenger will not have to pay for excess luggage?

parts.label: iii
parts.latex: What is the probability that a passenger will need to pay \$200, or more, in excess luggage fees?

A die is loaded such that in a roll of a single die the chance of rolling a 1 is $\dfrac{x}{4}$, the chance of rolling a 2 is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ and the chance of rolling a 6 is $\dfrac{1}{4}(1-x)$. The chance of rolling the other numbers (3,4 or 5) remain one in 6.

Two such dice are rolled together and the numbers on the uppermost faces are added to obtain a total score for the roll.

The probability of the total score of the two dice being 7 can be expressed as $y=f(x)$

Find the probability of rolling a 1 in a single roll of a die if the probability of rolling a total of 7 with two dice is $\dfrac{5}{36}$.

solutions.latex:
$A=4\sin\theta+4\sin\theta\cos\theta$

$\dfrac{dA}{d\theta}=4\cos\theta+4\sin\theta(-\sin\theta)+4\cos\theta\cos\theta$

$=4\cos\theta-4(1-\cos^2\theta)+4\cos^2\theta$

$=8\cos^2\theta+4\cos\theta-4$

$4(2\cos^2\theta+\cos\theta-1)=0$ for max/min

$(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta+1)=0$

$\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$ or $\cos\theta=-1$

$0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ as a right angle triangle

$\therefore\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$ only

$\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

test $\dfrac{d^2A}{d\theta^2}=16\cos\theta(-\sin\theta)-4\sin\theta$

at $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$=16\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}\times-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}-4\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$=16\times\dfrac{1}{2}\times-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-4\times-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$=-4\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{3}$

$=-2\sqrt{3}<0$ $\therefore$ max when angle is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\therefore$ angle is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $60^\circ$ which maximises the area

Note: As it is a trig function, $\theta$ is in radians; this should be reflected in the students' solutions.

notes: Cover: Sydney Technical High School, 2025 Higher School Certificate Trial Examination, Mathematics Advanced (AT4, graduating 2025); matches expected label. Section I Q1-10 (10 marks), Section II Q11-35 (90 marks); cover marker box totals 10/23/20/25/22 agree. pdf page 5 is the Section II instruction page, page 26 blank, page 27 is Appendix 1 (standard normal table, referred to in Q27(iii) as 'the table on page 35') and was not cropped. Solutions are a scanned, handwritten marked copy (pdf pages 28-38, landscape two-up); MCQ key read from the shaded answer sheet (no working), so MCQ working is generated. Many parts have no mark breakdown in the guidelines; Q19 guideline shows (2) for a 3-mark question. Q35(ii) guideline slip transcribed as written: -4 x (-sqrt3/2) should be -4 x (sqrt3/2), giving -6sqrt3 not -2sqrt3 (conclusion unchanged). Q30(i) sign tables are partly illegible and were summarised. Blank answer grid for Q28(i) is answer space and not cropped. Paper typos kept: Q1 'velocity of it motion', Q4 'values if the most', Q10 'has and angle', Q17(ii) 'that that', Q28(ii) 'to have at the height ... to be least', Q16 'Evaluate ,'.
